reason: E2 shows Hf-containing alloy homogenizes under irradiation without precipitation, supporting the suppression premise, but it is for a different composition (W31Ta34Cr5V27Hf3) and thin film, not bulk. E1 and E3 provide baseline evidence for the unmodified alloy's precipitation and hardening, but no cited evidence supports the ODTT/SRO mechanism, the specific 5 at.% Hf level, or effectiveness in bulk fabrication.
premises: Hf addition disrupts Cr/V clustering by altering local chemical environments and lattice distortions
Hf addition raises the order-disorder transition temperature (ODTT) and modifies short-range order (SRO)
Hf addition suppresses precipitation without increasing irradiation hardening
The baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy exhibits Cr/V precipitation and negligible hardening at ~8 dpa, 1073 K
The proposed mechanism is effective in bulk-fabricated material, not just thin films
